findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so concurrent callers all reload the manifest
findings.body: `GetWebAssets` reads the cache under `RLock`, releases it, then takes the write `Lock` and unconditionally rebuilds `entryPointAssetsCache`. In non-Dev mode, N requests can arrive while the cache is still empty (for example at startup). All of them see `ret == nil`, queue on `Lock()`, and each in turn reopens and re-parses `assets-manifest.json`, overwriting the cache with a fresh pointer. If the CDN path were enabled, each would also make its own HTTP request while holding the exclusive lock. This adds avoidable I/O and latency, and different callers get different `*EntryPointAssets` instances. Fix: right after `Lock()`, check again `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` (double-checked locking), or use `sync.Once` / `singleflight` for the non-dev path.
